verdict.rationale: Foreloop's docs make contract approval the explicit gate before any agent work: "Nothing runs until a person approves a contract," and agents only claim approved tasks before opening PRs. Scope is defined through intentions with an agreed purpose and editable deliverables, and the task contract carries skills into the run. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, documentation of who may approve (role/permission controls for an engineering lead), and detail on how strictly the gate is enforced against locally run agents beyond the task-executor skill only pulling approved tasks.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can approve a task's scope and contract before an agent is allowed to modify the repository

citations.quote: Nothing runs until a person approves a contract. Approval is the only gate, and the gate is deliberate: an agent is about to change your repository.
That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
An intention adds an agreed purpose and editable deliverables when you need more clarity.
The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
